description.narrative: The development objective of the Sindh Agricultural Growth Project for Pakistan is to improve the productivity and market access of small and medium producers in important commodity value chains. The project comprises of three components. The first component, capacity building and institutional development will finance capacity building of producers through technology development, technology dissemination, training, and exposure. It includes following three sub-components: (i) capacity building of producers; (ii) modernization of extension services and agricultural research; and (iii) strategic planning for the agricultural sector. The second component, investment for agricultural growth will finance specific investments in the horticulture and dairy value chains and a targeted investment to reduce post-harvest loss among small-holder rice growers. It will also finance a demand driven innovation fund to support farmers and producers with technology innovations in the selected value chains. It includes following four sub-components: (i) horticulture value chains; (ii) rice post-harvest loss management; (iii) dairy value chain; and (iv) demand driven innovation fund. The third component, project management and monitoring and evaluation will finance costs for: (i) project management units (PMUs), project coordinator's office, and project implementation units (PIUs); (ii) third party monitoring; (iii) implementation of environment and social management framework (ESMF) and pest management plan (PMP) and development of social assessment; and (iv) rigorous impact evaluation to attribute causality to project interventions.
To improve the productivity and market access of small and medium producers in important commodity value chains.

title.narrative: Increase in yields for selected commodities by targeted beneficiaries ('000 tones)

comment.narrative:
<p><u>Agriculture crops<u>:</u> <em>Achievement is 100% of the target.</em></u>  The weighted average pre-project productivityof 7.78 tons/hectare is derived from baseline survey productivity and end-of-project area under different agriculture crops. The target is 9.34 tons/ha at 20% increase over baseline.  The weighted average productivity at end-of-project is 9.38 tons/hectare (100% achievement). </p>

<p>Individual crop productivity achievement is as follows: (a) chili: 93% of incremental target, and 99% of EOP target; (b) onions: 137% of incremental target, and 106% of EOP target; (c) rice: 71% of incremental target, and95% of EOP target; and (d) dates: 96% of incremental target, and 96% of EOP target.</p>

<p><u>Dairy<u>:</u> <em>Achievement is 225% of the target.</em></u>???????  The weighted average baseline milk yield (for cows and buffaloes) is 4.5 liters/day.  The target is 5.4 liters/day at 20% increase over baseline. The end-of-project weighted average milk yield is 6.52 liters/day.  This is 45% over the baseline yield.</p>

title.narrative: Percent increase in aggregate sales of selected commodities for targeted beneficiaries

comment.narrative:
<p><u>Agriculture crops<u><em>:</em></u><em> Almost fully achieved.</em></u> This metric is measured based on increase in sales volume.  Given the high inflation, crop prices have peaked and a value based metric would not convey the achievement realistically.  The baseline sale volume was estimated 1.110 million tons, and the target was set at 1.332 million tons (20% increase), or an incremental 222,000 tons. Actual aggregate sale volume at end-of-project is estimated at 1.337 million tons. Achievement is 102% of the incremental target and 100% of the EOP target for all crops. </p>

<p>Individual crop incremental sale volume achievement varies between 78% and 129%. This variation in sales volume from appraisal targets for individual commodities is notunexpected given that the area under different crops is market driven and is the result of commercial decisions taken by the farmers. While the chili, onion and rice producers increased their area, the date producers reduced the area somewhat, affecting both production and sale volumes. It is more meaningful to assess this indicator performance against aggregate crop sale volume target. The incremental achievement is 20.6% against the 20% target (or 102%).</p>

<p><u>Dairy:</u>???????<u><em> Over-achieved.</em></u> This metric is also measured based on increase in sales volume.  The baseline production was estimated at about 50,216 liters/day, and the target was set at 60,259 liters/day (20% incremental over baseline).  Actual sale volume at end-of-project is estimated at 102,557 liters/day, a 104% increase over baseline or 5 times the project target of 20% increase. </p>

title.narrative: Number of commodities for which special studies are available

comment.narrative: <p>Only one feasibility study was carried out by FAO for onions. While Terms of Reference were prepared for other commodities, the studies could not be initiated.</p>

<p>The actual number of training days were 9,465 training days for agriculture beneficiaries, and 1,035 training days formilk producers, totaling to 10,500 training days.  Women training days totaled to 1,571 days, with 1,109 days for agriculture and 462 days for livestock.   </p>

title.narrative: Number of farmers/producers who receive training and knowledge services (gender disaggregated)

comment.narrative: <p><u><em>Achieved.</em></u>  All 111,071 farmers and 6,800 milk producers received training and knowledge services.  Some beneficiaries received multiple trainings on a range of themes - for example, governance of MPG entities; women milk producers received a second round of awareness training; and some beneficiaries also received training on artificial insemination.  Actual number of women trained were 13,420 in agriculture and 2,835 in dairy.</p>

<p><u>Achievement:  </u><u><em>Nearly 100% of the target achieved.</em></u> The project target consisted of 112,000 beneficiaries for agriculture crops and 6,120 milk producers.  Actual achievement was 111,071 agriculture producers and 6,800 milk producers. Of the latter, 5,753 milk producers were organized into groups, and the remaining 1,047 milk producers benefited from training, veterinary care and other support services. </p>
<p>Of the 111,071 agriculture beneficiaries, women share was 13,420; out of the 6,800 milk producers, about 2,835 were women. This totals to 16,255 women or about 13.8% of the total project beneficiaries.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of farmers achieving 20% reduction of on-farm pre and post-harvest losses and wastage for selected commodities

comment.narrative: <p><u><em>Over-achieved.</em></u>  This indicator was difficult to compute because the reduction of pre- and post-harvest lossvaried across different crops for a variable proportion of the farmers.  For example, for onions, the share of farmers experiencing more than 20% pre-harvest loss reduced from 68% to 34% (a 50% reduction in number of beneficiaries); for post-harvest loss, the corresponding figures are 65% to 38% (a 42% reduction). The table in Efficacy section provides crop-wise details.  Overall, the share of farmers with more than 20% pre- and post-harvest loss in the pre-project period was between 65% and 70% (or about 70%) for the different crops.  At end-of-project, the share of farmers with more than 20% pre- and post-harvest loss had reduced to between 35% and 55% (or about 45%) for the different crops.  This yields a reduction of 36% in the farmers with more than 20% of pre- and post-harvest loss.</p>

title.narrative: Number of milk producers organized into groups (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative: <p><em><u>Substantially achieved.</u></em> The total number of milk producer beneficiaries were 6,800, and exceeded 6,120 target.  However, of the 6,800 beneficiaries, 5,753 milk producers were organized into groups (or 94% of the project target) and the remaining 1,047 producers benefited from training and other project interventions.  Women participation was targeted at 40%. At end-of-project, 2,416 women participated as milk producer groups' membership (or about 42%).</p>

title.narrative: Clients who have adopted an improved agr. technology promoted by the project

comment.narrative:
<p><u><em>Target exceeded.</em></u> The project targeted 50% of the beneficiaries adopting an improved technology in agriculture crops. Of the expected 112,000 producers, the target was about 56,000 producers.  No specific estimate was made for milk producers.  At end-of-project, it is estimated that about 70,000 agriculture producers adopted at least one improved technology; there were cases of farmers adopting multiple technologies.  Almost all 5,753 milk producers that were organized into groups benefited from veterinary care services, and about 2,600 received AI service too.  However, technology adoption wasconstrued as an improvement in the production process. The end-of-project survey indicated some 2,760 milk producers to have adopted at least one improved animal husbandry technology or practice.  </p>
<p>While there is a sub-indicator to reflect women farmers adopting improved technologies, there was no project target, and it was extremely difficult to collect data on this indicator at end-of-project.  As such, the gender-related sub-indicator remained unreported. </p>

title.narrative: User satisfaction of the modernized extension services (gender disaggregated)

comment.narrative: <p><u><em>Substantially achieved.</em></u>???????  In the end-of-project survey, about 72% of the agriculture beneficiaries and 82% of milk producers indicated satisfaction with project interventions, including the modernized extension services. This yields a weighted average satisfaction rate of about 73%.  The same satisfaction rate is used for women since no disaggregated data was available.  </p>

title.narrative: Percent of high grade produce of selected commodities by targeted beneficiaries

comment.narrative: <p><u><em>Over-achieved. </em></u> This indicator presented some difficulty in interpretation in terms of what constituted high quality produce (just A grade or A+B grade). The target was indicated as 20% of produce.  The baseline survey indicated that the three horticultural commodities already had A grade produce exceeding the 20% target (chili: 24%; onion: 39%; and date: 31%).  The ICRR team believed that the project would have achieved this indicator should the end-of-project A grade share of production exceed the baseline share.  Estimates of A grade share exceeded the baseline share for all three commodities: chili up from 24% to 29%; onion up from 39% to 40%; and date: up from 31% to 34%. More importantly, the share of B grade produce also increased significantly for all commodities (see Table in Efficacy section). Overall, C grade share in production reduced by 35% for chili, 42% for onion, and 25% for date.  Hence, this indicator is considered over-achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Approval and dissemination of the Sindh Agricultural Development Strategy developed

comment.narrative: <p><u><em>Achieved.</em></u>???????  The Sindh Agriculture Policy was approved by the provincial government Cabinet Committee in April 2018, about 9 months beyond the target date. </p>
